answers.question: My club mate runs 70 miles a week before a marathon. I'm thinking of doubling to 80 next week to catch up, running twice a day. Would that work?
answers.answer:
No, doubling to 80 miles would not work, and I would not do it. A jump that size is a common way to reach the start line injured or flat.

| Week | Miles |
| --- | --- |
| Aug 24 – 30 | 27 |
| Aug 31 – Sep 6 | 37 |
| Sep 7 – 13 | 53 |
| Sep 14 – 20 | 40 |
| Sep 21 – 27 (planned) | 43 |

Your biggest week so far was 53 miles, and it left your legs heavy for days. Eighty is about 50 percent above that and double last week. Fitness takes weeks to show up, so miles crammed in now will not turn into race fitness by Nov 1, but the strain will show up.

Your club mate's 70 comes from a long build, not from a number you can match in a week. You are not behind. A steady 40 to 45 miles, a long run up to about 20, and marathon-pace work give you a real shot at under 3:45.

Two-a-days add another problem: they remove the recovery between runs. You currently have two full rest days and every easy run is truly easy, and that is part of why you are feeling good. Keep that.

new.analysis:
## How last week went

Last week followed the plan closely: every run landed within a few hundredths of a mile of the planned distance. That matters because the week before ran well over the plan, so this was a clean week of doing what was written. Your legs felt heavy early on, which is a normal cost after a big week, and they were fine by Thursday with no pain at all.

The marathon-pace session was well executed. You held about 8:35/mi for 6 miles, which is the pace a 3:45 needs, and it felt like effort 7/10. The long run was even from start to finish, with the back half 1 second per mile faster than the front. That is good pacing.

## Why next week is built this way

Next week steps up by about 3 miles, roughly 7 percent, which is a safe size for growth. The extra miles go into a slightly longer Thursday and a longer Sunday. Thursday works as the medium-length run of the week, and Sunday gets its first marathon-pace finish.

I chose threshold work on Wednesday and marathon pace on Sunday so the two hard efforts sit four days apart. The other three runs stay truly easy. Threshold work raises the pace you can hold comfortably, and the Sunday finish teaches you to hold goal pace on tired legs, which is the main skill in the last 6 miles of a marathon.

## Reading the heart-rate numbers

Your easy share last week was about 64 percent, below the 80 percent target, but that is expected with a marathon-pace session in the week. Warm-up, cool-down and the pace block all count as harder time. The long run also drifted into zone 3 in its second half even at effort 5/10, which is normal drift over 15 miles.

Your easy runs themselves sit in zone 2 at 139 bpm, and that is what I care about. Next week has two quality sessions again, so expect a similar share.

## Where this sits before the race

You are 5 weeks out from the race, so there is room for one more big long run, around 19 to 20 miles, before the taper begins. After that the plan turns toward freshness, because the fitness you can still add is small and the freshness you can lose is large. That is also why extra miles now cost more than they give.
